Apex Legends throws out the `CM_*` & `TRICOLL_*` physics systems
Their replacement lives in `BVH_NODES` & `BVH_LEAF_DATA`
`rmdl` uses the same system as `bsp`, though they tend to use different parts of the format

## BVH

The `BVH_*` system appears to be the final evolution of Earl's physics engine[^simd]
`BVH4` stands for Bounding Volume Hierarchy w/ 4 children per-node

Earl's **Extreme SIMD** talk seems to align best w/ Apex Legends, but Elements are present across all ~3 Engines
(TF:O has broken physics & Apex is still evolving, but 1 Engine per game makes sense to me)

### BVH Lumps

A `BVHNode` can index into `BVHLeafData`, when it's type is given
Each type enum selects a handler function and feeds it some context + the pointer into `BVHLeafData`

`BVHLeafData` ends up being a combination of different data types all squished together
So far we have identified a few types, but not necessarily how they function, or how to replicate them.

[^simd]: GDC on Youtube: [Extreme SIMD: Optimized Collision Detection in Titanfall](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BIfqfC1i7U)

nodes.body:
Some notes stolen from @r-ex

Only ever seen up to leaf type 0-7. or well, child type 0-7

### Child Types
 0 - BVH4 node
 1 - no child
 2 - (unk, nullsub)
 3 - (unk, points to other leaves)
 4 - unpacked vert tri (bsp)
 5 - packed vert tri (rmdl)
 6 - unpacked vert quad (bsp)
 7 - packed vert quad (rmdl)

Only difference between 4-5 and 6-7 is that:
 - one uses packed vertices (int16 with a scale factor of sorts to scale it up to the right value)
 - one uses regular float3s

`bsp`s can technically use packed vertices tho i dont think any do
But while most `rmdl`s use packed vertices, i have seen some that don't

The decision to use packed/unpacked is based on the physical size of the model (i.e., how big it appears in the world)
If the coordinates are very large then they will lose meaningful levels of accuracy by being packed, so they must be raw floats

found 8 & 9
9 is actually fairly common

8 is the same as the `*coll` keyvalues in r5 trigger entities
some r5 `.bsp`s have `PACKED_VERTICES` tho very few

Looks like type 9 is Static Props
Screencap from r-ex:
![rexx_bvh_leaf_9_static_prop](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/5762068a-db1e-46dd-bed3-4166902d1c5b)
type 3 is an array of leaves, something like `CMGeoSet` vs `CMPrimitive`

more stolen from @r-ex 

we recently got pretty decent coverage on BVH nodes/leaf data in respawn-mdl templates for RMDL collision data
the data itself is not overly complicated but i am no closer to figuring out how to properly re-create it

![bvhleafdata_5_raw](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/8f0231e6-f4d6-4805-9e5b-60ee8e19e211)

purple data at the top is packed vertices, dark yellow is the first 4 bytes of leaf type 5 (packed triangles)
next bytes are some indices into the vertex data for each tri
each tri leaf can have more than one tri
not sure what their strategy is for when these are split/created tho unfortunately

![bvhleafdata_5](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/912d5f9b-ea6a-47ed-9444-3a83138ef019)

`BVHLeaf5Triangle` looks quite similar to `TricollTriangle`, but with more bits for indices & smaller flags

```c++
struct { uint32_t A: 10, B: 7, C: 7, flags: 8; } TricollTriangle;
```

Found a way to show how many of each `BVHLeafType` is present in a given `.bsp`:
```python
>>> import bsp_tool, os, fnmatch
>>> r5s3md = "E:/Mod/ApexLegends/season3/3dec19/maps"
>>> maps = {m[:-4]: bsp_tool.load_bsp(os.path.join(r5s3md, m))
...         for m in fnmatch.filter(os.listdir(r5s3md), "*.bsp")}
>>> children = lambda n: (n.index.child0.child0_type, n.index.child0.child1_type,
...                       n.index.child1.child2_type, n.index.child1.child3_type)
>>> lc = [c.value for n in maps["mp_lobby"].BVH_NODES for c in children(n)]
>>> {print(f"{x:02X} {lc.count(x):>5}") for x in sorted(set(lc))}
00 11951
01    41
02     3
04     1
```
